reading.body:
Xiaomi holds 4,220 granted US patents and one listed AI product, the MiMo foundation model, which carries a cross-border data review advisory.

The patent count is large but the recent grants are not AI infrastructure. They cover positioning, wireless communication, a folding mechanism, a monitor design, and communication methods. This is the patent portfolio of a device manufacturer, not of a company building data centers or power capacity. The one AI asset in the record is a model, and the only note attached to it is a data-handling caution rather than a compute figure.

For AI scaling, the relevant question is where training and inference run and what feeds them. Nothing here reports Xiaomi's compute, its buildings, or its power arrangements. A foundation model implies some training footprint, but the data does not size it, so no claim about Xiaomi's draw on the grid can be made from this record.

The record is also thin in coverage. It counts US grants matching the applicant phrase "xiaomi" since 2001 and lists five recent ones, so it says nothing about filings elsewhere, nothing about pending applications, and nothing about how many of the 4,220 relate to AI at all. The MiMo entry is a single product line with a single advisory note. Treat this as a company identity record with a patent tally, not as evidence about AI capacity.
